ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), S.C. 2000, c. 17; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Alberta Corporate Registry (via accredited service provider) or foreign equivalent registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Canada is a Hague Apostille Convention member; apostille issued by Global Affairs Canada or provincial designated authority; for Spanish/Chinese documents, consular legalization in source country may be required if not apostille-eligible)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of Passport / Government ID of each beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority or relevant government of residence/citizenship

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against Canadian consolidated list of financially sanctioned persons (Global Affairs Canada), Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) guidance on politically exposed persons (PEPs), the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, and the US OFAC SDN List for any cross-border USD or dual-listed activities. Enhanced due diligence required for PEPs, family members, close associates, and individuals from FATF high-risk jurisdictions. Director/UBO adverse media check and sanctions screening to be completed within 5 business days prior to incorporation and refreshed at least annually.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (ACR) via authorized registry services – actual portal: 'CORES - Corporate Registry System' accessible through provincial accredited service providers (e.g., Alberta Registries / Registry Agents); direct link: https://www.alberta.ca/business-registry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Business name must be in English, French, or romanized transliteration; the legal name in the certificate must be in a Latin-script alphabet (without diacritical marks beyond standard Canadian usage). If a non-Latin script is used concurrently, a romanized transliteration must be submitted and must match the certificate exactly. The name must not contain symbols or punctuation prohibited by the Alberta Business Corporations Act (e.g., no @, #, $, % unless part of a recognized professional designation).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Auditor (unless licensed under provincial professional acts)
Corporation / Inc. / Ltd. / ULC / Unlimited (must be legally accurate as to actual entity type)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a Name Reservation Request (NUA) is rejected by the Alberta Corporate Registry, the applicant may: (1) submit a revised NUA with a new primary and alternate name (no statutory waiting period); (2) file a written appeal/formal reconsideration with the Director of Names under Alberta Business Corporations Act and the Business Names Registration Act, providing evidence of prior use, trade-mark registration, or consent from objecting party; (3) appeal a final administrative refusal to the Court of Queen's Bench of Alberta (now Court of King's Bench of Alberta) within 30 days of issuance of the refusal; (4) for trade-mark related objections, file an opposition before the Canadian Intellectual Property Office (CIPO) or Federal Court where applicable. Extension of an approved name reservation is allowed once for an additional 30 days, subject to service provider fees, provided no intervening conflict.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is permissible for the registered office only if the virtual address is a physical street address in Alberta (P.O. boxes are prohibited) and the registered office service provider agrees to accept service of process and maintain statutory records. For an Unlimited Liability Corporation (ULC) engaging in ESG carbon accounting/audit services, a virtual-only presence may create commercial-substance risk for federal tax treaty benefits, provincial tax registrations, and registrations with the Alberta Information and Privacy Commissioner. Regulatory expectations for this industry (management consulting and carbon advisory) require a substantive local presence (at least one Canada-resident director is not statutorily required for a ULC, but for GST/HST and income tax purposes, a permanent establishment in Alberta is beneficial). Industry best practice and CRA administrative policy prescribe a physical operational office for audit-support and client fiduciary duties.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 0.25 quantified risk (low-moderate) for standard low-risk advisory business; however, unannounced physical on-site inspection may occur: (a) during a Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) compliance audit; (b) during a FINTRAC or provincial securities examination if the entity expands into brokerage activities not clearly exempt; (c) during automatically triggered review if the company claims Alberta Research and Innovation tax credits or carbon-offset brokerage registration. Probability assessed at 15–20% over first 24 months for a low-risk advisory entity, rising to above 40% if the entity acts as a carbon offset broker holding client funds.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c. B-9, as amended, ss. 1-10, 15, 25, 102-103 (unlimited liability corporations); initial filing under Alberta Corporate Registry administration
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, Government of Alberta
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation and Articles of Incorporation (Form 01); Certificate of Incorporation issued upon filing
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; no escrow account is required under Alberta law; authorized share capital and issued paid-up capital are determined by the articles and board resolution
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the corporation accept the subscription for 1,000 common shares at CAD 1.00 per share, as set out in the register of members, and that the board allot and issue such shares to the subscribers. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the corporation be established at the address described in its Notice of Registered Office, and that such notice be executed and filed as required by the Business Corporations Act (Alberta). RESOLVED, that [Name] be President, [Name] be Secretary, and [Name] be Chief Financial Officer, each to serve until resignation or removal, and that the President and CFO be authorized jointly to operate bank accounts and execute contracts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry online via Service Alberta registries portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a mandatory NUANS name search for the proposed corporation; if a distinctive name is used, reserve the name; if a numbered company is preferred, obtain a staggered number from the Alberta Corporate Registry and adopt the style 'Alberta Unlimited Liability Corporation'.
required_dossiers: Name Reservation Certificate (if using a proposed name)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as confusingly similar, select an amended name, file a revised NUANS search, and resubmit the reservation without additional statutory waiting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting Articles of Incorporation and Statutory Notices
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (prepared by incorporator or authorized agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare Articles of Incorporation in Form 01 for an unlimited liability corporation, including registered office address in Alberta, directors, authorized share structure, and any restrictions on businesses. Complete the Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry questions the articles, file a clarification or corrected Form 01 within the deficiency period; an appeal lies to the Registrar if the filing is refused.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (online filing portal or authorized registry agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed Application for Incorporation, Articles of Incorporation, Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors, and pay the applicable incorporation fee. Upon successful review, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, correct the specific deficiency in a resubmission, provide supporting declarations, and pay any updated fee; if refused, request reconsideration from the Alberta Corporate Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting and First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational meeting or execute written resolutions in lieu of meeting. Adopt corporate by-laws, approve the pro-forma first board resolution covering share subscription, registered office, officer appointments and banking authorities, then issue share certificates and open the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Minutes of organizational meeting or written consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director or officer is absent or signature is defective, cure by obtaining unanimous written consent of all directors or calling a adjourned meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office and Resident Agent Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry and building/landlord administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify the registered office address is a physical street address in Alberta and that the landlord or premises owner consents to use of the address. If the address changes after incorporation, file a Change of Registered Office notice.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered office is found non-compliant, file a Change of Registered Office Notice and provide the registry with the corrected street address.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax Registration and Business Number Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a federal Business Number (BN) and register for Alberta corporate income tax obligations, GST/HST, payroll and any required corporate reports. For a ULC, consider executing a ULC tax status election with CRA to achieve pass-through treatment if applicable under the Canadian Income Tax Act.
required_dossiers: Notice of Directors with residential addresses
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA rejects the BN application for incomplete director information, provide the missing consents and resubmit; a representative identifier (RepID) and signed authorization cure deficiency.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing authority applies; the business is office-based professional services under ISIC 7020, not a manufacturing or physical industrial operation.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None: no sectoral operating permit or manufacturing license is required for ESG carbon accounting, advisory and offset brokerage services in Alberta.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (for any incidental emissions or waste, and general EPBA compliance)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – office-only administrative operation; no mandatory Full EIA Report or Environmental Assessment Registration under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act (Alberta).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No regulated industrial wastewater discharge or VOC point-source emissions; any minor office waste must be disposed through municipal and commercial waste contractors in compliance with Alberta Waste Management Regulation. Carbon offset brokerage activities do not trigger site discharge standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain a fire safety certificate from the municipal fire marshal for the leased office space under the Alberta Fire Code; confirm structural load inspections by the landlord for office occupancy; and conduct an Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) compliance review for workstations, egress routes and first-aid requirements in accordance with the OHS Act (Alberta).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); primary online services include CRA My Business Account and Business Registration Online (BRO). Alberta corporate-law registration is administered separately by Alberta Registry agents and is not a tax registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Alberta ULC generally obtains a CRA Business Number (BN), a nine-digit identifier, and applicable program accounts. Incorporation or registration may generate a BN; otherwise apply through BRO or submit CRA Form RC1. Register for a corporation income tax program account (RC) and, when required, a GST/HST program account (RT). A non-resident carrying on business in Canada should apply for the required BN and accounts through BRO or the CRA non-resident registration process. Provide the entity's legal name, Alberta incorporation or registration details, registered address, activities, fiscal year-end, directors, and authorized representative information. A BN does not itself establish tax residence or satisfy all filing obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: An Alberta ULC is a Canadian corporation and is generally taxed as a corporation under the Income Tax Act (Canada); it is not a Canadian pass-through entity and has no Canadian check-the-box election to become a partnership or disregarded entity. A qualifying ULC may be treated as disregarded or as a partnership for United States federal income tax purposes by an eligible entity election under US Treasury Regulations, but that election does not alter its Canadian classification and may produce cross-border hybrid-mismatch consequences. Canadian corporate residence, provincial allocation, and any treaty relief require separate analysis.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST), with Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) applying in participating provinces; Alberta has no provincial sales tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in taxable supplies (including zero-rated supplies) in a single calendar quarter or over four consecutive calendar quarters for a small supplier, subject to statutory aggregation and related-person rules. A non-resident carrying on business in Canada may be required to register under the regular regime without relying on the small-supplier threshold. Separate simplified-regime rules generally use a CAD 30,000 threshold over a 12-month period for specified cross-border digital products, services, and goods supplied to Canadian consumers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no general federal real-time e-invoice clearance, tax API submission, or digital-stamping mandate for ordinary GST supplies. GST registrants must provide prescribed invoice or receipt information when required and retain books and records in an accessible, readable form; electronic records must be available to the CRA on request. Certain public-sector procurement or contractual arrangements may impose separate electronic invoicing requirements.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods may be zero-rated when the statutory export conditions are met and the supplier retains evidence that the goods were exported. Services supplied to a non-resident may be zero-rated under the applicable Excise Tax Act provisions, subject to exclusions, including specified services relating to real property situated in Canada, tangible personal property situated in Canada, and certain services performed in Canada in respect of goods. Carbon-accounting or ESG advisory services are not automatically zero-rated: determine the recipient's residence, the actual recipient and use of the service, and whether an exclusion applies. Zero-rated supplies remain taxable supplies for registration and input tax credit purposes. Refunds are generally claimed through input tax credits on required GST/HST returns, subject to documentation and statutory limitation periods.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export declaration or other applicable Canada Border Services Agency export reporting evidence, where required
Commercial invoice, purchase order, and shipping or transport records identifying the goods and foreign destination
Bill of lading, air waybill, courier record, or other carrier proof of export, as applicable
Evidence of foreign recipient and delivery outside Canada
For exported services, contract, invoices, proof of recipient non-residence, service records, and evidence supporting the applicable zero-rating provision
Bank or payment records supporting the transaction; an Inward Remittance Certificate is not a generally prescribed Canadian GST export document
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada imposes no general foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds. The CRA may deny zero-rating or input tax credits where statutory conditions or supporting records are not established, assess tax, interest, and applicable penalties, and reassess within the applicable limitation period or later where statutory exceptions apply, including misrepresentation attributable to neglect, carelessness, wilful default, or fraud. False statements or omissions may attract penalties under the Income Tax Act or Excise Tax Act, including gross-negligence penalties where applicable; fraud may also result in prosecution. No fixed export-zero-rating penalty or automatic clawback applies solely because an export claim is challenged.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) — monetary authority and lender of last resort; banking prudential supervision is delegated to OSFI (Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions) under the Bank Act; AML/CFT administration is vested in FINTRAC (Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA). Canada operates a free-floating exchange-rate regime and maintains no foreign-exchange control authority; the Exchange Control Act was repealed in 1951.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible on both current and capital account, consistent with Canada's long-standing IMF Article VIII obligations. There are no exchange-control permits, surrender rules, or repatriation restrictions on capital injections, dividends, interest, royalties, or trade proceeds. A non-resident shareholder of an Alberta ULC may remit profits freely, subject only to Part XIII withholding tax under the federal Income Tax Act (statutory 25% on dividends, reduced by applicable tax treaty — e.g., 5% under the Canada–US Treaty for a 90%-owned subsidiary, 15% otherwise) and to standard commercial banking documentation. The ULC's partnership-style pass-through eligibility does not alter the Part XIII analysis, and no Bank of Canada or CRA advance approval is required for any remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory timeline, no minimum conversion ratio, and no mandatory surrender of export proceeds or any other foreign-currency receipts. An exporter may retain foreign currency (USD, EUR, etc.) indefinitely in a Schedule I bank foreign-currency account, convert to CAD at a commercially negotiated spot rate, or apply the proceeds directly to foreign trade payables. FINTRAC EFT reporting applies only to record-keeping thresholds (CAD 10,000 or more per transaction), not to exchange-control conversion.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Low for primary treasury; Medium only for ancillary cross-border payout corridors. Canada does not issue EU/UK-style Electronic Money Institution (EMI) licences. Offshore digital EMIs cannot obtain a Bank Act Schedule I licence, cannot hold demand deposits at the Bank of Canada, and lack direct access to Canadian clearing systems (Lynx, ACSS, Real-Time Rail). A foreign EMI may at best sponsor a Canadian bank account or register as a FINTRAC money services business (MSB) and, where applicable, as a Retail Payment Service Provider (RPSP) under the Bank of Canada-administered Retail Payment Activities Act. For an Alberta ULC, an unlicensed offshore EMI is not viable for payroll, CRA tax remittances, or LC operations; Canadian tax obligations must settle through a Canadian bank or an MSA/RPSP-approved PSP.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-person attendance is not statutorily mandated, but a live identity-and-authority interview (in-branch or via bank-approved dual-process video conferencing) with at least one Director and all authorised signatories is effectively required for a non-resident-owned ULC. Fully remote opening without any interview is unavailable for ULC structures; where permitted, the bank requires a notarised Certificate of Status from the Alberta Corporate Registry, an Alberta-registered head office or place of business, certified resolutions, a certificate of incumbency, proof of registered agent/counsel, and documentary evidence of every ultimate beneficial owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through taxation and unlimited liability structure obscure the economic substance, creditor-rights allocation, and ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) of the shareholder base.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Alberta incorporation or continuance documents; recent Certificate of Status from the Alberta Corporate Registry; registered and records addresses; unanimous shareholder agreement; complete UBO chain with trust deeds, partnership agreements, or nominee declarations for every non-individual shareholder; corporate register of directors; Alberta legal opinion on ULC nature and creditor-rights consequences; notarised identity documents for all directors and 25%+ beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident controllers with no Canadian nexus (no payroll, no physical office, no CRA activity) trigger heightened source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta lease or virtual-office agreement; business plan detailing ESG carbon audit and offset brokerage pipeline; CRA business number (BN) and GST/HST registration; payroll remittance evidence if any employee registered in Canada; net-worth and source-of-funds statements for shareholders injecting more than CAD 100,000; certified board resolutions; bank reference letters from the foreign parent's home-jurisdiction bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Carbon offset brokerage involves receipt and onward payment of third-party settlement funds, which may be mischaracterised as unlicensed money services business activity or unexplained electronic fund transfer (EFT) flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master client agreements and offset purchase/sale contracts; registry statements from the Alberta Emission Offset System or recognised voluntary standards (Verra, Gold Standard); invoice and settlement trail for each transaction; project-level technical due diligence reports; written confirmation from the bank's compliance team that the ULC is not acting as an MSB; annual audited financial statements segregating escrow/float balances from operating capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency cross-border EFTs for consulting and audit fees with no tangible goods movement are typical of invoice-matching fraud; bank compliance may defer or block wires pending review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed engagement letters and ISIC 7020 service agreements; deliverable-based work papers and time records; scope-of-work and audit opinion drafts; client identity files; wire instructions on company letterhead; explicit purpose narrative in each SWIFT field 70; periodic independent treasury compliance review to demonstrate a stable transaction profile.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity injections from a non-resident parent or shareholder are executed by SWIFT MT103 (or MT202/MT202COV where an intermediary bank is used) to the ULC's CAD account at a Schedule I bank. The beneficiary account uses the Canadian institution number (3 digits), transit/branch number (5 digits), and account number (e.g., RBC institution '003', Calgary transit '000XX'). The payment narrative must state 'Shareholder capital contribution / equity injection into [ULC legal name]' to prevent misclassification. No Canadian exchange-control filing or CRA clearance is required; the receiving bank records the transaction for FINTRAC EFT reporting when the value is CAD 10,000 or more. The ULC must book the receipt as stated capital or contributed surplus, supported by a board resolution, an updated share register, and, where shares are issued, a certificate of allotment filed with the Alberta Corporate Registry. USD-denominated injections may be converted at the bank's spot rate or credited to a USD settlement account and cleared through CLS/CHIPS; no statutory conversion into CAD is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements use four principal rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 for cross-border supplier, client, and carbon-credit settlement payments, with full beneficiary account details and descriptive remittance information; (2) Lynx, Canada's high-value payment system (successor to LVTS), for CAD payments of CAD 500,000 or more, providing real-time finality; (3) the Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) for lower-value CAD ACH-style credits and pre-authorized debits; and (4) commercial letters of credit opened or confirmed by a Schedule I bank in Calgary or Edmonton under UCP 600 and ISBP 745, together with documentary collections under URC 522 when appropriate. For USD settlements, Canadian Schedule I banks clear through their US branch networks and CHIPS/Fedwire membership. All outbound wires are subject to FINTRAC record-keeping, Canadian sanctions screening under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act, and OSFI's third-party/correspondent banking compliance expectations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD outright forwards (maturity-matched to invoices, LC maturities, and dividend cycles)
Spot FX contracts and FX swaps/rollovers with Schedule I dealing banks
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a Credit Support Annex
Plain-vanilla and barrier FX options (CAD calls/puts) for conditional exposure hedging
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on non-CAD emerging-market currencies (e.g., CNY, INR, BRL) for offset-brokerage exposures in restricted-convertibility jurisdictions
Exchange-traded CAD/USD futures and options on CME or ICE for collateralised hedging without bank credit-line utilisation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return (Corporate Registry Declaration of Registered Office, Directors, and Shareholders)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First filing due within 15 months of incorporation; thereafter due within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 50 applies; continued failure to correct annual return defaults for two or more consecutive years may lead to administrative dissolution under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) and resulting loss of legal standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Corporate Income Tax Return (Form T2)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the corporation's tax year-end; calendar-year corporations must file by June 30 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of the balance owing plus 1% per full month for up to 12 months; directors may be subject to director liability assessments and continuous non-filing may lead to forced administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Treasury Board and Finance / Alberta Revenue
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end, matching the federal T2 due date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of the greater of CAD 25 and 5% of any unpaid amount, with daily interest accrual; prolonged default exposures may trigger collection and registration cancellation proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Return (where the corporation is an annual filer)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Three months after the fiscal year-end for an annual filer; calendar-year filers must file by March 31.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file results in a late-filing penalty calculated at 1% of the annual net tax payable plus 25% of the portion exceeding CAD 10,000; repeated non-filing may result in criminal prosecution and mandatory registration revocation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, a private non-distributing corporation is exempt from independent audit only if all shareholders unanimously waive the auditor requirement in accordance with s. 163. Audit is compulsory if shares are distributed to the public, if shareholders holding 5% or more of voting shares demand an audit, or if the Directors cannot establish the unanimous-consent waiver. The ULC's unlimited liability structure does not eliminate this statutory audit requirement unless the unanimous shareholder waiver is validly obtained each year.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for entities with public accountability; Canadian Private Enterprise GAAP (ASPE) for the private ULC engaged in ESG/carbon auditing. The corporation may elect either framework on a consistent basis, but ASPE is the typical baseline for a private unlimited liability company headquartered in Alberta.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta's annual return does not require a standalone UBO filing; however, the ULC must maintain a Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta). The ISC register must be updated within 15 days of any share transfer or end of significant control, and must be available for inspection; the annual return must nevertheless be signed with confirmation of the current registered office, directors, and corporate records, and any share transfer affecting significant control must be noted in the register before annual attestation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CAD 250 - 900 (USD 190 - 690) depending on Calgary or Edmonton physical office, registered-agent service, or premium corporate-management provider.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: CAD 3,500 - 8,500 (USD 2,600 - 6,400) for a small-to-mid-size private ULC, absent auditor waiver; review-engagement fees for ULCs providing carbon-audit advisory services typically range from CAD 1,500 to 3,500.
